title: Slide layouts

steps.say: Text and a chart stacked on one slide: the chart is pushed off the bottom, out of sight. A slide has a fixed size, unlike a page.
.columns with two .column divs puts the words beside the chart. Widths are shares of the slide: 40% and 60%.
A tabset works on slides too. Here the Jazan tab is open; the Kingdom is one click away, so one slide holds both charts.

title: "Unemployment in the regions"
subtitle: "Quarterly briefing · synthetic data"
format: revealjs
---

```{r}
#| include: false
library(tidyverse)
rates <- read_csv("unemployment.csv")
kingdom <- rates |> filter(region == "Kingdom")
jazan <- rates |> filter(region == "Jazan")
change <- rates |>
  filter(region != "Kingdom") |>
  group_by(region) |>
  summarise(change = last(rate) - first(rate))
up <- change |> filter(change > 0) |> pull(region)
```

## Unemployment is falling

- Down in `r sum(change$change < 0)` of `r nrow(change)` regions since 2022
- It rose only in `r up`

## The national trend

```{r}
ggplot(kingdom, aes(date, rate)) + geom_line()
```
